metadata.title: Our team
metadata.description: Researchers, visiting colleagues, project students and alumni of the Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab.

intro: We bring together robotics, machine learning and bioengineering to study adaptive physical intelligence across scales. Explore our researchers’ backgrounds, research directions and selected work, meet the 2026 project cohort, and discover the contributions of our alumni.

data.name: Dr Dandan Zhang
data.affiliation: Department of Bioengineering · Imperial College London
data.research: Adaptive physical intelligence for dexterous manipulation across scales
data.description: Dandan is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Bioengineering at Imperial College London and founder of the Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab. Her research connects tactile sensing, robot learning, shared autonomy and optical and magnetic microrobotics.
background: Assistant Professor, Imperial College London · joined in 2023
Previously Lecturer in Robotics at the University of Bristol
PhD in Medical Robotics, Imperial College London · 2021
data.researchApproach: The lab studies how robots can combine sensing, learning and physical interaction to manipulate objects across scales. Tactile intelligence and adaptive control connect dexterous manipulation with medical robotics and optical and magnetic microrobots.

selectedWorks.title: A vision-based tactile sensor with in-sensor computing paradigm for seamless tactile sensing and perception
Embodied Cross-Domain Intelligence in Biomedical Microrobots: A Review

data.name: Wen Fan
data.description: Wen develops vision-based tactile sensors and learning methods that connect robotic touch with physical understanding. His work brings together sensor design, manufacturing and tactile perception for manipulation.
data.affiliation: Department of Bioengineering · Imperial College London
data.project: Learning object-centric physical properties from robotic touch for efficient perception and manipulation
background: MSc, University of Manchester · 2021
Research assistant at Bristol Robotics Laboratory from 2022, before moving his doctoral research to Imperial
data.researchApproach: His doctoral project asks how a robot can infer object properties through touch and use that information during manipulation. Related work connects tactile-sensor design, in-sensor computation and multimodal learning for contact-rich tasks.

selectedWorks.title: A vision-based tactile sensor with in-sensor computing paradigm for seamless tactile sensing and perception
i-Tac: Inverse Design of 3D-Printed Tactile Elastomers with Tuneable Optical and Mechanical Properties
ADM-DP: Adaptive Dynamic Modality Diffusion Policy through Vision-Tactile-Graph Fusion for Multi-Agent Manipulation

data.name: Jialin Lin
data.description: Jialin studies magnetic microrobots, imaging and adaptation between simulation and experiments. His research connects microrobot perception and control with potential biomedical applications.
data.affiliation: Department of Bioengineering · Imperial College London
data.project: Adaptive sim-to-real algorithms for magnetic microrobots using ultrasound imaging
background: MSc in Robotics, University of Bristol · 2022
BEng in Mechanical Engineering, Dalian University of Technology · 2021
data.researchApproach: The project investigates how ultrasound observations can guide magnetic microrobots as control algorithms transfer from simulation to experiments. Related work examines reconfigurable electromagnetic actuation and modular millirobot locomotion.

selectedWorks.title: DexterousMag: A Reconfigurable Electromagnetic Actuation System for Miniature Helical Robot
Design and Control of Modular Magnetic Millirobots for Multimodal Locomotion and Shape Reconfiguration

data.name: Lan Wei
data.description: Lan develops machine-learning methods for optical microrobot perception, including diffusion-based image generation and transfer between simulation and experiments. Her doctoral research also explores collaborative control.
data.affiliation: Department of Bioengineering · Imperial College London
data.project: Towards autonomous optical microrobots through perception, collaborative control and deployment
background: ME in Computer Science, University of Science and Technology of China · 2024
BE in Computer Science, Xiamen University · 2021
data.researchApproach: Her research aims to recover depth and pose information from microscope images while reducing the gap between simulated and experimental data. Diffusion-based image generation and physics-informed estimation connect visual perception with microrobot control.

selectedWorks.title: Dual-Control Frequency-Aware Diffusion Model for Depth-Dependent Optical Microrobot Microscopy Image Generation
Physics-Informed Machine Learning with Adaptive Grids for Optical Microrobot Depth Estimation
TacVerse: A Multisensor Dataset and Benchmark for Cross-Sensor Vision-Based Tactile Perception

data.name: Zongcai Tan
data.description: Zongcai studies machine-learning methods for the design and control of optical microrobots. His doctoral project focuses on physics-informed control for biomedical research settings.
data.affiliation: Department of Bioengineering · Imperial College London
data.project: Physics-informed machine learning for optical microrobot control in biomedical applications
background: MRes in Medical Robotics and Image-Guided Intervention, Imperial College London · 2024
BE in Vehicle Engineering, Jilin University · 2022
MRes research on human–robot shared control for optical manipulation with haptic guidance
data.researchApproach: His work connects physics-informed learning with optical microrobot perception and control. It also explores virtual visuo-haptic interaction, using a digital twin to link operator guidance with complex-shaped optical microrobots.

selectedWorks.title: A Digital Twin Framework for Virtual Visuo-Haptic Teleoperation of Complex-Shaped Optical Microrobots
Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Efficient Sim-to-Real Data Augmentation in Micro-Object Pose Estimation

data.name: Kangyi Lu
data.description: Kangyi investigates physics-informed AI for autonomous microrobots and dexterous manipulation in lab-on-a-chip environments. She also contributes to project supervision on shared control for magnetic microrobot navigation.
data.affiliation: Department of Bioengineering · Imperial College London
data.project: Physics-informed AI for autonomous microrobots and dexterous micromanipulation in lab-on-a-chip systems
background: ME in Electronic Information, Shanghai Jiao Tong University · 2024
BE in Automation, Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics · 2021
data.researchApproach: The project brings together physical models, microscopic perception and learned control for autonomous micromanipulation. Related work considers shared control and language-conditioned bimanual manipulation with magnetic microrobots.

selectedWorks.title: Micro-Dexterity in Biological Micromanipulation: Embodiment, Perception, and Control
Mag-VLA: Vision-Language-Action Model for Bimanual Magnetically Actuated Microrobot Manipulation

data.name: Piotr Blaszyk
data.affiliation: Department of Bioengineering · Imperial College London
data.research: AI for healthcare and surgical context awareness
data.project: Multimodal large language models for surgical context awareness
data.description: Piotr investigates how multimodal large language models can support surgical context awareness. His research also connects simulation, tactile perception and interpretable learning for robot-assisted palpation.
background: Earlier MRes project on sim-to-real transfer learning for robotic manipulation
Contributes research support to uncertainty-aware surgical skill assessment
data.researchApproach: His doctoral project asks how visual and language information can help robotic systems interpret surgical tasks and context. Related open research uses a calibrated digital twin and graph-based learning to investigate shallow-vessel localisation from tactile palpation.

selectedWorks.title: Toward Trustworthy Robot-Assisted Sliding Palpation for Shallow Vessel Localisation with a Calibrated Digital Twin

data.name: Nitirak Rayabphand
data.description: Nitirak studies magnetic microscale robotics for medical applications at the University of Bristol. His work spans magnetic swarm control and the fabrication of active microstructures.
data.project: Magnetic swarm robotics
data.supervision: Sabine Hauert (main supervisor) and Dandan Zhang (co-supervisor)
background: Master’s degree in Robotics Engineering, Osaka University · 2022
BE in Mechatronic Engineering, King Mongkut’s University of Technology Thonburi · 2015
data.researchApproach: His research explores fabrication and magnetic actuation as connected parts of microrobot design. The Magni-DOME work combines light-based fabrication and magnetic control to produce and study diverse active microstructures.

selectedWorks.title: Rapid Parallel Fabrication and Control of Diverse Microrobotic Structures with Magnetic Functionalization
Magni-DOME: An Open Platform for High-Resolution Light-Based and Magnetic Contactless Fabrication of Active Microstructures

data.name: Qiming Liu
data.affiliation: Visiting from Shanghai Jiao Tong University
data.description: Qiming is a visiting postdoctoral researcher from Shanghai Jiao Tong University, with research interests in robot learning, manipulation and navigation. He contributes to project supervision on personalised robotic assistants and language-model approaches to manipulation.
background: PhD, Shanghai Jiao Tong University
BEng, Shanghai Jiao Tong University
data.researchApproach: His project mentoring connects high-level language instructions with practical robot actions. Current projects explore how robotic assistants can account for user preferences and how hierarchical planning can support manipulation in cluttered environments.

data.name: Yongchen Wang
data.project: Human–robot shared control for magnetic microrobot navigation
data.projectContext: The project investigates how a person and an automated controller can share control of magnetic microrobots. The aim is to combine operator intent with navigation assistance during delicate microscale manipulation.

selectedWorks.title: Context-Aware Adaptive Shared Control for Magnetically-Driven Bimanual Dexterous Micromanipulation
Mag-VLA: Vision-Language-Action Model for Bimanual Magnetically Actuated Microrobot Manipulation

data.name: Yacui Zhao
data.project: Tactile-informed reinforcement-learning fine-tuning for flow-based vision–language–action models
data.projectContext: This project studies how touch feedback can refine a vision–language–action policy through reinforcement learning. It focuses on adapting a flow-based model to physical contact during manipulation.

data.name: Xinyu Zheng
data.project: Adaptive multimodal imitation through a real-to-sim-to-real learning pipeline
data.projectContext: The aim is to learn from demonstrations across real and simulated environments, then adapt the policy back to the physical robot. Combining multiple sensing modalities is intended to support more transferable manipulation skills.

data.name: Zhidan She
data.project: Learning physical properties using object-centric representations, vision–language-model priors and robotic tactile feedback through learnable implicit modelling
data.projectContext: This project explores how visual and language priors can be combined with touch to infer an object’s physical properties. It aims to build an object-centred representation that can be updated through interaction.

data.name: Haotian Jiang
data.project: Multimodal-large-language-model-driven multi-robot collaboration with real-time self-correction
data.projectContext: The project explores how a multimodal language model can coordinate multiple robots while monitoring their progress. It asks how the team should correct its actions when observations diverge from the plan.

data.name: Liang Wang
data.project: Multi-robot collaborative control with multimodal large language models and dynamic task allocation
data.projectContext: This project examines how task descriptions and sensory information can be used to assign work across a robot team. It focuses on updating those assignments as the task or environment changes.

data.name: Mu Xing
data.project: Trustworthy multimodal large language models for uncertainty-aware surgical skill assessment
data.projectContext: The project investigates multimodal models for assessing surgical skill while expressing uncertainty. Its aim is to make the model’s confidence and limitations visible alongside the assessment.

data.name: Zhouxuan Xia
data.project: Intelligent surgical multimodal frameworks for autonomous robot-assisted surgery, skill analysis and scene understanding
data.projectContext: The project connects surgical scene understanding with analysis of procedural skill and robot-assisted actions. It explores how multimodal information could support a shared representation of the task and its context.

data.name: Xinyuan Dou
data.project: Personalised robotic assistants empowered by large language models
data.projectContext: The project explores how a robotic assistant can interpret language requests while accounting for a person’s preferences. It examines the connection between personalised task understanding and executable robot actions.

data.name: Junlin Wu
data.project: Hierarchical language models for robotic manipulation in cluttered environments
data.projectContext: The project studies a hierarchy of language-based reasoning and robot action for manipulating objects in clutter. It asks how a broad instruction can be broken into feasible steps and adjusted to the observed scene.

data.name: Gaus Sayyad
data.project: Multimodal control of a wearable dual-arm robotic system for assisted object manipulation
data.projectContext: This project explores wearable interfaces for coordinating two robot arms during assisted object manipulation. Combining interaction modalities is intended to make bimanual control more intuitive and responsive to the user.

data.name: Sherlyn Ong
data.project: Personalised robotic assistants empowered by large language models
data.projectContext: This project investigates how large language models can support personalisation in a robotic assistant. It considers how the assistant can relate a user’s request and preferences to the actions available to the robot.

data.name: Erin Sarlak
data.project: Multi-robot collaborative control with multimodal large language models and dynamic task allocation
data.projectContext: The project explores how multimodal large language models can help a team of robots divide and coordinate its work. Dynamic task allocation is studied as a way to respond to changing tasks and observations.

data.name: Jonathan Wachsmuth
data.project: Decoding the metabolic drivers of cancer metastasis using machine learning
data.projectContext: This project applies machine learning to questions about metabolism and cancer metastasis. The aim is to identify patterns that help investigate how metabolic processes relate to cancer spread.

data.name: Samuel Parsons
data.project: Vision-based tactile sensing for 3D contact deformation and dense distributed-force reconstruction
data.projectContext: The project studies how images from a tactile sensor can reveal three-dimensional contact deformation and distributed forces. It links sensor observations to a spatial description of physical interaction.

data.name: Jessica Mead
data.project: Mechanical characteristics of tactile sensors with functionally graded material for medical palpation
data.projectContext: This project examines how varying material properties within a tactile sensor affects its mechanical response. The application is medical palpation, with an emphasis on how sensor construction shapes contact measurements.

data.name: Yulan Fei
data.project: Deep learning for microrobot depth and pose estimation
data.projectContext: The project explores deep-learning approaches for estimating a microrobot’s depth and pose from observations. The aim is to improve spatial perception for subsequent micromanipulation and control.

groupprojects.name: Synaptech
groupprojects.project: Design, simulation, fabrication and control of a soft robotic gripper
groupprojects.projectContext: The project brings mechanical design, simulation, fabrication and control into one soft-gripper development process. The aim is to connect the gripper’s physical construction with how it deforms and interacts with objects.

data.name: Qingzheng Cong
data.description: Qingzheng contributed to tactile perception, haptic interaction and soft robotic manipulation during his time as a research assistant. His co-authored work includes multimodal sensing, tactile benchmarking and sensor-integrated grippers.
data.research: Tactile perception, haptics and soft robotic manipulation
background: MSc in Biorobotics, University of Bristol · 2023
BE in Mechanical Engineering, Durham University · 2022
data.researchApproach: His research connected tactile-sensor hardware with perception and manipulation. The selected work below spans cross-sensor tactile representations and multimodal sensing for contact-rich interaction.

data.description: Ziyuan visited from Zhejiang University of Technology from December 2024 to December 2025. His visit focused on data-driven control for tactile servoing in robot-assisted bed-bathing applications.

data.researchApproach: The visit project investigated how tactile feedback can inform robot motion during physical assistance. It connected data-driven control with the need to regulate contact in a medical-robotics setting.
